proposed_from.topic: Sharp directed-fan-in frontier for numerical edge identification in confounded linear SEMs. Input: an acyclic mixed graph, rational feasible positive-definite covariance, and a queried directed coefficient; the fiber consists of all supported structural matrices whose induced noise covariance respects the bidirected graph. Prove a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm at maximum directed indegree one using Möbius components plus singular 2-SAT clauses, returning a unique rational value, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. Prove promise universal-real completeness at indegree two via a fiber-bijective private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler with rational strictly diagonally dominant covariance. Preserve MIIVsem as the numerical-identification consumer and treat covariance-confidence-set inversion as secondary. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: indegree-one bi-affine equations were reduced to invertible Möbius components with quadratic-or-cofinite domains and singular equality disjunctions; indegree-two addition, multiplication, copying, repeated inputs, covariance-slot separation, and positive-definite witnesses passed bounded exact checks over 48 Möbius relations, 2,286 singular assignments, and two complete compilers. A global primitive element can have exponential degree, so certificates must remain componentwise quadratic. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: independently audit the arbitrary-input component normalization and 2-SAT equivalence, including poles and every singular degeneration, then verify a complete selector-circuit compiler. EARLY KILL TEST: compare the full component algorithm against real-algebraic elimination on bounded degenerate rational systems and eliminate every copy equation in a circuit using all primitives; any extra fiber branch kills the frontier. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_fanin_numedge_frontier.md.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 2, Lemma 3, Corollary 4, Theorem 14, and Section 8
seed_details.opportunity: Determine the smallest maximum directed indegree at which covariance-specific numerical edge identification changes from exact polynomial-bit solvability to promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the unrestricted storage node in the hardness reduction by private-parent, occurrence-hub gates, and replace generic elimination on the tractable side by a pole-aware pointwise normal form.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for bounded-indegree numerical identifiability, fan-in-one Möbius normalization, and fan-in-two fiber-preserving hardness found no occupied target--method pair; the nearest results remain unrestricted numerical hardness and tree-shaped generic identification.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call the result immediate from the unrestricted reduction and the generic tree algorithm.
seed_details.rebuttal: Neither source controls the published reduction's unbounded storage fan-in, and generic polynomial identity arguments explicitly omit the singular covariance strata that create poles, rank-one disjunctions, and global branch consistency.

seed_details.opportunity: Turn the generic one-, two-, or infinite-solution classification for directed trees into a deterministic exact algorithm for every feasible rational covariance on arbitrary directed forests of maximum indegree one.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After composing the rank-two bilinear relations, retain every finite pole and factor every rank-one relation at the supplied covariance instead of applying polynomial identity testing over a generic parameter field.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: The exact target--method search found numerical algebraic geometry and generic TreeID implementations, but no singularity-complete Möbius-plus-Boolean fiber algorithm.
seed_details.red_team: The forest extension could be dismissed as a routine restatement of the tree proof.
seed_details.rebuttal: The novelty is pointwise completeness on the exceptional covariance locus: singular relations couple otherwise independent components through disjunctions, a phenomenon absent from the generic tree proof.

seed_details.opportunity: Prove promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness when every sink has at most two directed parents and the supplied rational covariance is strictly diagonally dominant with a known feasible witness.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the common variable-storage sink by singleton masters, gate-local occurrence sinks, and two-step equality hubs whose covariance slots are pairwise private.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: The bounded-fan-in and strictly-diagonally-dominant restriction was not present in the published reduction or in the retrieved low-indegree identification papers.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may regard bounded-fan-in conversion as the usual arithmetic-circuit normalization.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary circuit normalization does not preserve the entire SEM fiber, prevent extra coefficient branches, isolate covariance slots, or certify a rational positive-definite covariance; those are the reduction's load-bearing steps.

seed_details.opportunity: Transfer an exact numerical fiber audit through the latent-to-observed transformation and return either a unique MIIV target coefficient or two observationally equivalent latent-SEM witnesses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic instrumental-set rank validity after latent-to-observed transformation by a fiber-level correspondence at the realized covariance, including scaling choices and singular first stages.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: MIIVsem documentation and latent-to-observed identification papers provide equation-level estimators and generic equivalences, not complete pointwise fiber certificates.
seed_details.red_team: The graphical latent-to-observed equivalence might make the audit a software wrapper around an existing theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published equivalence is between identification criteria; it does not show bijection of exceptional numerical fibers or transport alternative feasible parameter witnesses.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1, its perturbation induction, and Section 6
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the local condition number and the limit law of a numerically identified coefficient along sequences approaching a Möbius pole, a repeated quadratic root, or a fiber bifurcation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global sufficient matrix-norm recursion by a stratum-specific derivative or root expansion of the exact component recovery map.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Robust-identification bounds, conditional-IV variance formulas, and regular half-trek influence functions were found, but none covers changes in numerical fiber cardinality.
seed_details.red_team: This may reduce to a routine delta method away from singularities.
seed_details.rebuttal: The proposed content is precisely the nonregular boundary where the derivative diverges or a repeated root invalidates the ordinary delta method.

seed_details.anchor_location: Definition of fractional affine square-root terms and Theorem 27
seed_details.opportunity: Establish polynomial-size componentwise quadratic certificates and an exponential lower bound against a single global primitive-element encoding for low-fan-in numerical fibers.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Pass from one shared square-root expression on a generic component to independent quadratic fields across pointwise connected components.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: The retrieved SEM papers specify symbolic low-degree expressions but do not analyze certificate length under composita of independent quadratic fields.
seed_details.red_team: The exponential field-degree example is elementary algebraic number theory rather than causal identification.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is essential to a correct polynomial-bit output theorem, but it is best retained as a supporting proposition rather than the paper's kernel.

seed_details.opportunity: Give an exact covariance-stratum characterization of when a queried fan-in-one edge has one, two, or cofinitely many attainable real values.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the missing-cycle resultant, which can introduce a spurious root, by component normalization plus a Boolean extendibility test for every candidate root.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Missing-cycle papers classify generic solutions and selected path graphs; no retrieved result gives the full pointwise cardinality stratification for arbitrary fan-in-one mixed graphs.
seed_details.red_team: The trichotomy could be only a repackaging of the quadratic formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: Multiple singular relations couple components, and the cofinite-versus-at-most-two conclusion uses exact \(2\)-CNF extendibility and majority closure, not a single quadratic equation.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 2 and the programmable missing-edge equation in Equation (11)
seed_details.opportunity: Classify numerical edge identification when only \(k\) vertices have directed indegree two, interpolating between the polynomial fan-in-one class and unrestricted fan-in-two hardness.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Expose the coefficients incident to the \(k\) two-parent vertices and conditionally reduce the residual system to the fan-in-one Möbius and \(2\)-CNF normal form.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: No fixed-parameter or fixed-number-of-two-parent-vertices result was found for numerical SEM fibers.
seed_details.red_team: The unrestricted hardness theorem may already use only a constant number of two-parent vertices.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published construction uses a storage node with growing fan-in, while the proposed compiler uses a growing number of two-parent gates; whether a fixed number suffices remains genuinely open.

seed_details.anchor_location: Definition of the covariance-to-parameter condition number, Theorem 1, and Section 6
seed_details.opportunity: Invert a finite-sample covariance confidence region through the exact fan-in-one fiber algorithm to obtain a confidence set that can split or become unbounded near singular strata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace point perturbation bounds by uniform semialgebraic projection over a covariance confidence region.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Near-singular SEM regularization and robust-identification papers do not provide exact confidence-set inversion through a changing-cardinality coefficient fiber.
seed_details.red_team: Confidence-set inversion is automatic once the population algorithm exists.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage is automatic only for an exact covariance region; computational tractability and uniform behavior at bifurcations are separate, unresolved results, so this remains secondary.
